headline: NHC gives the Southwestern Gulf of America disturbance a 90% chance of forming within 7 days (90% within 48 hours). No advisories or forecast track yet.

gulf.text: Showers and thunderstorms are showing signs of organization in association with a broad area of low pressure located over the southwestern Gulf of America. Continued development of this system is expected, and a tropical depression is anticipated to form over the next day or so while it drifts eastward. The low pressure area could bring gusty winds and areas of heavy rain to the western portions of the Yucatan Peninsula of Mexico in a couple of days. The disturbance is expected to turn to the north or northeast toward the northern Gulf Coast by the end of the week. It is still too early to determine specific impacts to the northern Gulf Coast, but interests from the Florida Panhandle to Louisiana should closely monitor the progress of this system. The NOAA Gulfstream is scheduled to sample the environment over the Gulf later today and an Air Force reconnaissance aircraft is scheduled to investigate the system tomorrow.
gulf.source: NHC outlook, 800 AM EDT Tue Oct 6 2026

google.text: 11 of 50 ensemble members forecast a track so far. 9 of 11 bring the center to the Louisiana-to-Florida coast (FL 6, AL 2, MS 1), typically around Fri, Oct 9, 1 PM CT. 9 of 11 reach hurricane strength (7 major); typical peak 99 kt.
